ETag.description: The entity's version, the strong validator for `If-Match` (docs/adr/0050 D2)

SetCookie.description:
The session cookie `__Host-cowork-session`: `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax;

The login's state cookie `__Host-cowork-oidc`: `HttpOnly; Secure;
SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=600`. It holds the `state`, the `nonce`, the
PKCE verifier, `return_to` and the time, sealed with AES-256-GCM under a key
derived from `COWORK_SESSION_KEY` (docs/adr/0029 D1); the callback reads it

FilterHasOpenQuestions.description: Whether the ticket has an open question (docs/adr/0049 D1)

ChatMessage.description:
One message of a conversation, in the neutral model the backend translates for its provider. A
`user` message carries `text`, what the person wrote; an `assistant` message `text`, what the model
said, and `tool_calls`, the calls it made — at least one of the two; a `tool` message
`tool_call_id`, the call it answers, `ok`, and `text`, the answer the model read. There is no
system message: the backend writes the model's instructions on every turn (docs/adr/0076).

Each is told in their inbox (`mentioned`) and watches the ticket while the comment stands. The

Dashboard.description:
The team's dashboard, the nine fixed tiles of docs/adr/0018 D6, read in one read-only
transaction. Every tile counts only what the caller can see: the visibility predicate holds
each ticket, question and time entry it reads, so a restricted project or a confidential
ticket the caller cannot see counts nowhere and is named nowhere (docs/adr/0034 D4,
docs/adr/0065 D4), and a time entry follows the visibility of time as well (docs/adr/0034
D5). A deleted ticket counts nowhere either — nor its questions and its time — until it is
restored (docs/adr/0024 D1). *Open* is every state but `done` and `dropped`. The open tiles count the tickets as they
stand at the request; throughput and lead time end with the period's last day; the time is
the period's (docs/adr/0019 D2). Days are UTC days and weeks ISO weeks of them
(docs/adr/0055 D3). The counted projects are the ones the `project` filter names, or, without
a plain value, every project the caller sees that is not archived; a negated value leaves its
project out, and a key that names no project the caller sees counts nothing.

age.description:
Tile 5, the age distribution of the open tickets, the age being the time since filing
(`opened_at`) at the request: five buckets in this order, every one present — under 7
days, 7 to under 30, 30 to under 90, 90 to under 365, and 365 days or more, a day being
24 hours.

open_by_severity.description:
Tile 2, open tickets by severity: every severity of docs/adr/0010 D1 in its order,
`critical` first, with the count of open tickets that carry it, zero included.

open_by_state.description:
Tile 1, open tickets by state: the open tickets of each counted project per state, by
project key; a project and state without an open ticket is left out. Their sum per state
is the tile, their sum per project the project's open count.

recent.description:
Beside the tiles, kept from the front page before the dashboard: the eight open tickets of
the counted projects updated last, newest first (the later id on a tie).

security.description:
Tile 3, open security findings: `live`, then `boundary` (docs/adr/0010 D1, D2), each with
the count of open tickets of that class and the oldest of them by filing (`opened_at`, the
earlier id on a tie), `null` while there is none.

throughput.description:
Tile 6, throughput: the tickets done per ISO week (docs/adr/0019 D2) for the eight weeks
that end with the one holding the period's last day, oldest first, every week present. A
ticket counts in the week of its `done_at` while it is done: one reopened since counts
nowhere, one done again counts once, in the week of its last done. The last week counts
up to the period's last day.

DashboardAgeBucket.description: The open tickets whose age is at least `from_days` and under `to_days`

to_days.description: Null for the last bucket, which has no upper bound

DashboardBlocked.description:
Tile 4, blocked tickets: the count of open tickets in the state `blocked`, and the one blocked
longest with its block's kind (docs/adr/0009 D2) — blocked since its latest recorded
transition into `blocked` (docs/adr/0026), or since its last update where no act records one;
the earlier id on a tie. `oldest` is `null` while none is blocked.

DashboardDecisions.description:
Tile 8, open decisions: the count of open questions (docs/adr/0011 D3) on the tickets of the
counted projects, whomever they are asked of and whatever state the ticket is in, and the one
asked first, the earlier id on a tie; `oldest` is `null` while none is open.

DashboardLeadTime.description:
Tile 7, lead time: the median time from filing to done (`opened_at` to `done_at`) of the
tickets done in the thirty days that end with the period's last day — done now, their
`done_at` in that window, as throughput counts them; the median of an even count is the mean
of the middle two. `median_seconds` is `null` while no ticket was done in the window.

done.description: The tickets the median is taken over

to.description: The window's last day, the period's

DashboardPeriod.description:
The period the request named, or the default: the thirty days that end today, UTC. Both days
are inclusive.

oldest.description: The oldest open ticket of the class; `since` is its filing

DashboardTicket.description: A ticket a tile names, with the time the tile measures it from

DashboardTime.description:
Tile 9, time booked in the period by project: the minutes of the time entries whose day lies
in the period, voided ones left out (docs/adr/0017 D7), per counted project that has any, by
project key; only the entries the caller may see count (docs/adr/0034 D5).

bearerToken.description:
A personal access token, `cwk_` and 43 base62 characters
(docs/adr/0035 D1). `X-Cowork-Agent: name/model/session` marks the
request as an agent's; a token with the agent flag is an agent's
with or without it, and no header removes the flag (docs/adr/0036).
A request that carries an `Authorization` header is a token's, and
its cookie, if any, is not looked at. A token of a person the identity
provider's groups no longer admit is refused with `401 not_allowed`,
checked against the person's groups as of their last login or groups
refresh, at most `COWORK_OIDC_GROUPS_REFRESH` apart, and so is one whose
groups are older than `COWORK_OIDC_GROUPS_MAX_AGE`, until the person
signs in to the browser once (docs/adr/0035 D8).

sessionCookie.description:
The session of a browser login: an opaque id of 256 random bits, set
by `POST /auth/local` or `GET /auth/callback` as `HttpOnly; Secure;
SameSite=Lax; Path=/` (docs/adr/0031 D2). A session acts as its
person with no agent flag and with the whole of the person's role: it
has no scope of its own. An `X-Cowork-Agent` header makes its request
an agent's — the capabilities the person chose for the chat
(`GET /api/v1/me/chat`), the agent rules, the mark on its acts — and
refuses it what only a session does with `403 agent_forbidden`
(docs/adr/0036 D3, docs/adr/0043 D5); the chat marks its tool calls so
(docs/adr/0076).
Its writes are held to the CSRF check of docs/adr/0037 D1: `Origin`
(or `Referer`) equal to the installation's `COWORK_BASE_URL` and
`X-Requested-With: cowork`.
sessionCookie.name: __Host-cowork-session

info.description:
A multi-team backlog for people and the agents that work for them.

Every route that names a person is authenticated with one of two
credentials. A personal access token, `Authorization: Bearer cwk_…`
(docs/adr/0035), is for scripts and agents; the session cookie of a
browser login (docs/adr/0031 — `POST /auth/local`, or the identity
provider's `GET /auth/callback`, docs/adr/0029) is for the UI. Each
operation says which it takes: most take either, a few a session only —
creating a token, a team or a local account, resetting or changing a
password, logging out, a turn of the chat and stopping one, choosing the
chat's capabilities, a global administrator's list of every team, purging a
deleted ticket — the one irreversible act on a ticket —, removing the
orphaned objects a consistency check found — gone for good as well —, and the
administration acts that give access: adding a member, setting a grant,
making or changing a group mapping, restricting or opening a project,
putting a person on its access list. A request of a session that writes must come from the installation's
origin and carry `X-Requested-With: cowork` (docs/adr/0037). A request
marked as an agent's — by the token's agent flag, or by an `X-Cowork-Agent:
name/model/session` header — is bound by the agent rules
(docs/adr/0036, 0043). Errors are RFC 9457 problem details with a stable
`code` (docs/adr/0047).

get.description:
"Assigned to me" (docs/adr/0018 D3): every ticket that is neither `done` nor `dropped` and is
assigned to the person, in every team they belong to, each with its team and its place in
its project's rank — one read per team (docs/adr/0021 D5), under the same predicate as the
team's own lists. Ordered by the score (docs/adr/0014 D5) — highest first, a ticket without
one last — then by the ticket's id; the place is the secondary indicator. Cursor paging only
(docs/adr/0048 D3). A token restricted to a team reads that team, one restricted to a
project that project (docs/adr/0035 D3).

get.description:
The chat acts as the person's agent, and its requests hold exactly this set
(docs/adr/0043 D5, docs/adr/0076): an act that needs another capability is refused
to the chat with `403 agent_forbidden` and stays the person's. A person who never chose
holds the default — every capability but `decide`, `close`, `drop` and `record-answer` —,
and `chosen` is false.

put.description:
Only the person, in a browser session: what the chat may do is access to the person's
teams, which a token does not give (`403 session_required`, docs/adr/0035 D5), and a session
the agent header marks — the chat itself among them — is `403 agent_forbidden`. The set
replaces the one before, from the chat's next request on, a running turn's included; an empty
set leaves the chat the baseline (docs/adr/0043 D4). No `If-Match`: the person is the only
writer, and the same set sent twice changes nothing (docs/adr/0050 D4). A change is recorded
as the person's act.

get.description:
"Open decisions" (docs/adr/0018 D3): the open questions asked of the person and those open in
their teams — asked of nobody (docs/adr/0011 D2) —, on tickets they see, each with its
team and its ticket; one read per team (docs/adr/0021 D5). Ordered by the score of the
ticket (docs/adr/0014 D5) — a `done` or `dropped` ticket, which has none, after the scored ones
— then by the ticket's id and the question's number. Cursor paging only (docs/adr/0048 D3). A
restricted token reads as on `GET /api/v1/me/assigned`.

200.description: A page of the open decisions

get.summary: The open decisions of the person, across their teams

get.description:
One inbox per person, a union over the teams they belong to — one read per team, never one
query across them (docs/adr/0020 D1, docs/adr/0021 D5). A notification is written by the act
that caused it, for the events of docs/adr/0020 D2: a ticket assigned to the person, a
question asked of them, a question they asked answered, a state change of — or a comment on —
a ticket they watch (docs/adr/0013 D6: a stake, the assignee, the reporter, an open question
asked by or of them), a ticket that blocks one they watch reaching `done` or `dropped`, and an
`urgent` stake on a ticket assigned to them. Their own acts and their agents' tell them
nothing. Each entry names its team beside the ticket and renders from the act (D3): the
ticket as it is now, the act as the ticket's activity shows it — without its payload where
it names a ticket the person cannot see — and whether the comment or question it is on has
been withdrawn since. A notification of a ticket the person no longer sees, or of a team
they left, is absent and counts nowhere (docs/adr/0065 D5).

`unread` counts the person's unread notifications in the teams the request reaches. A
token restricted to a team reads that team's, one restricted to a project that project's
(docs/adr/0035 D3). Cursor paging only; the cursor holds the place, so a notification that
arrives while the person reads shifts nothing (docs/adr/0048 D3).

get.summary: The person's notifications across their teams, newest first

put.description:
"Mark all read" (docs/adr/0020 D6): every unread notification of the person up to and
including `through`, in the teams the request reaches; one that arrived after it stays
unread. One act `read` per team where something changed; none where nothing did. Needs
`write` scope. Read notifications are kept ninety days, unread ones until they are read.

put.description:
Recorded as the act `read`; one already read changes nothing and records nothing. A
notification that is not the person's, or of a ticket they no longer see, is `404 not_found`.
Needs `write` scope.

"Next for me" (docs/adr/0018 D3 as amended 2026-10-05): every ticket that is neither `done` nor
`dropped` and is assigned to the person or to nobody, in the projects they see of every team
they belong to, each with its team and its place in its project's rank — one read per team
(docs/adr/0021 D5), under the same predicate as the team's own lists. Another person's ticket
is not in it. Ordered by the score (docs/adr/0014 D5) — highest first, a ticket without one
last — then by the ticket's id; the place is the secondary indicator. Cursor paging only
(docs/adr/0048 D3); the cursor carries the score's key and the id. `project` narrows to one
project of the team `team` names. A token restricted to a team reads that team, one
restricted to a project that project (docs/adr/0035 D3).

Needs the current password, which counts like a login attempt towards
the lockout of the account and the throttle of the client's address —
`429 too_many_attempts` with `Retry-After` before it is hashed
(docs/adr/0033 D6). The new one must be as long
as `COWORK_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH` and differ from the current one; every
other session of the account ends (D4), and a temporary password is no
longer temporary. The local administrator's password is set by the
configuration and cannot be changed here (`403 forbidden`).

get.description:
Every project the person sees in every team they belong to, each with its team — the lists
of the UI's sidebar (docs/adr/0023 D2, D4) —: one read per team (docs/adr/0021 D5), under the
predicate of `GET /api/v1/teams/{team}/projects`, so a restricted project is listed only to
the team's administrators and the people on its access list (docs/adr/0034 D3). An archived
project is left out, and so is a team in which a global administrator holds no role
(docs/adr/0034 D2). Ordered by the team's slug, then the project's key. Cursor paging only,
without a total (docs/adr/0048 D3). `team` narrows to one of the person's teams. A token
restricted to a team reads that team's projects, one restricted to a project that project
(docs/adr/0035 D3).

get.summary: The projects of the person's teams, across their teams

get.description:
Normalises each `remote` to its identity, host/path (docs/adr/0066 D1), and
searches the projects the caller sees in every team of the person — a
restricted token in its own team and project only (docs/adr/0035 D3). The
remotes are tried in the order given, `origin` first by convention; the
first one with a binding decides, and of its bindings those whose
sub-directory covers `path`, the most specific first. One binding is
`bound`; several are `ambiguous`, a data error the person resolves
(docs/adr/0066 D6); none is `unbound`, with a proposal for a project made
from the first remote that has an identity (D2): the team — the only one
the caller may create projects in, else the one that binds repositories
under the same owner, else the list to choose from — a key from the
repository's name, free in each team offered, and the name itself. A
caller who may create a project nowhere gets no proposal and the reason.
A remote that names no host is reported with a null identity. Send no
credentials: cowork stores none, and a proxy's log may carry the query.

The search of `GET /api/v1/teams/{team}/search` over every team the person belongs to —
one read per team, never one query across them (docs/adr/0021 D5) — merged by rank; each hit
names its team. `team` narrows to one of them. A token restricted to a team searches that
team, one restricted to a project that project (docs/adr/0035 D3). A global administrator
without a role in a team searches nothing of it (docs/adr/0034 D2).

The token's metadata as the list shows it, the key of the project it is
restricted to, and the request's mark: whether it is an agent's — by the
token's flag or by an `X-Cowork-Agent` header (docs/adr/0036 D2, D3) — the
agent recorded on its acts, and the capabilities it holds
(docs/adr/0043 D4). The MCP server reads it at start to tell the model what
it may do (D6), and `cowork-mcp token check` to tell a person
(docs/adr/0070 D2). A browser session presents no token: `404 not_found`.

Metadata only; a token's plaintext is shown once, at creation
(docs/adr/0035 D1, D6). Newest first, paged by cursor, or by number with
a total (docs/adr/0048 D2).

post.description:
Only the person themselves, in a browser session: no token creates a
token (`403 session_required`) and no administrator creates one for
another person (docs/adr/0035 D5). The answer carries the plaintext
`token` once; cowork stores its SHA-256 only (D1).

The lifetime is `lifetime_days`, by default `COWORK_TOKEN_DEFAULT_LIFETIME`
(90 days) and at most `COWORK_TOKEN_MAX_LIFETIME` (one year): a longer
one is shortened to the maximum, and `expires_at` in the answer says what
the token got (D4). An agent token has at most `write` scope
(docs/adr/0036 D5), carries capabilities and nothing else does, and gets
every capability when `capabilities` is left out; an empty list is no
capability, the baseline only (docs/adr/0043 D4). A team
restriction needs a team the person belongs to, a project restriction a
project of it the person sees; either, if not, is `validation_failed`
without saying which of the two it was.

An `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry create nothing twice, but the stored
answer never holds the plaintext (docs/adr/0045 D6): the repetition
answers the token without `token`, and the person revokes it and makes
another.

201.description: The token, with its plaintext once

delete.description:
Immediate and recorded; the row stays listed (docs/adr/0035 D6). A
token may always revoke itself; revoking another token of the person
needs `write` scope, and an agent may revoke only the token it holds
(docs/adr/0043 D3). Revoking a revoked token changes nothing.
delete.summary: Revoke one of the person's tokens

The optional binding file of a repository without a remote or of a fork
(docs/adr/0066 D4): `team` — or its deprecated name `tenant`, read for one
release — and `project`, and optionally `path` — the
sub-directory of a monorepo it binds — and `url`, the installation it
belongs to. Unauthenticated, so an editor can load it.

get.description:
Every team by slug, with the role the caller holds in it — the highest
of their mapping and their grant — or `null` where they hold none
(docs/adr/0034 D2). It is how a global administrator finds a team in
which they have no role: there they see its administration — the
team and its settings, its members, its group mappings — and grant
themselves a role (`PUT …/members/{person_id}/grant` with their own id),
and nothing of its work until they have. A person who is not a global
administrator is `403 forbidden`; the teams they belong to are in
`GET /api/v1/me`. A browser session only, which no agent mark carries: a
token is `403 session_required`, so a leaked token of a global
administrator lists no team beyond the person's own.

200.description: A page of teams, by slug

get.summary: Every team of the installation, for a global administrator

post.description:
A global administrator, in a browser session: no token creates a team
(`403 session_required`), and a person who is not a global administrator
is `403 forbidden`. The creator becomes the team's first administrator
by a marked grant, recorded with the team (docs/adr/0032 D7); a global
administrator has no other role in it (docs/adr/0034 D2). The slug is
immutable and never reused (docs/adr/0005 D4).

Every member reads it; a global administrator who holds no role in the
team too, in a browser session, as part of its administration
(docs/adr/0034 D2).

patch.description:
An administrator's act with `admin` scope; agents never (docs/adr/0043 D3).
`If-Match` is required (docs/adr/0050 D3).

A change that widens what the members may see or do — switching
`time_visible_to_members` or `members_create_projects` on, or moving
`time_locked_until` earlier or clearing it — takes a browser session: a
token is `403 session_required` (docs/adr/0035 D5). The other direction,
and the name, stay open to an administrator's token.

200.description: A page of accounts, by person id

get.summary: The local accounts the team manages

post.description:
The administrator sets a temporary password; the person changes it at the
first login, before anything else (docs/adr/0033 D4). The account gets a
marked grant with the given role in this team (docs/adr/0030 D3) and
is managed by this team. There is no registration and no invitation:
this route is the gate (D1). A username is unique in the installation,
so `409 username_taken` also tells an administrator that another team
has the name.

A browser session only: a token, an administrator's included, answers
`403 session_required`. An account made with a leaked token would
survive the token's revocation, and so would the password the
administrator chose.

put.description:
The person can no longer log in, their tokens are revoked and their
sessions end (docs/adr/0024 D5); the person and every act they made stay.
Not for the administrator's own account (`403 forbidden`). Deactivating a
deactivated account changes nothing. A deactivation that would leave the
team without an administrator who can log in is `409 last_admin` and
changes nothing (docs/adr/0034 D1); it takes the team's lock, so two

What the daily check found last: the files whose metadata is there and whose bytes the bucket
lacks — dangling, after a restore that brought the database back without them; their download
answers 404 saying so — and the objects under the team's prefix that no metadata names —
orphans, after a restore that brought the bucket back from a later point, or a removal that
failed. The counts are exact, the lists at most 1000 entries each. The team's administrators,
a token's `read` scope; anybody else is `403 forbidden`, because the lists name files of tickets
they may not see. Before the first check `check_id` is null. Beside the check, when a project
of the team or the whole team was last exported — the second line of its backup
(docs/adr/0059 D2) —, null before the first. An answer the client holds unchanged is `304` to
its weak `ETag` (docs/adr/0054 D7).

post.description:

docs/adr/0043 D3): the missing files of the check's list nobody accepted yet count as accepted
from now on — as lost — instead of dangling, and no longer hold the alert. Nothing is removed:
the files stay listed on their tickets and their download answers 404 saying the bytes are
missing; one whose bytes come back is whole again, and a later loss of it counts once more. The
body names the check whose list the administrator was shown; a newer check is
`409 consistency_check_stale`. Recorded as `accepted`, with the count. A list with nothing to
accept changes nothing and records nothing.

post.description:

check whose list the administrator confirms; a newer check, or a removal confirmed already, is
`409 consistency_check_stale`. Each orphan of that list is asked again whether an attachment
names it now — one that does is kept —, the act is recorded as `purged`, with the counts and no
key, and the objects are removed after the commit; a removal that fails is logged with its key
and listed again by the next check. A check with no orphans changes nothing and records
nothing. Without object storage, `501 uploads_disabled`.

get.description:
For every member of the team. The chat is available when the installation configures at
least one provider (`COWORK_CHAT_PROVIDERS`); `providers` lists them in the configured order,
the first being the one a turn uses when it names none. Otherwise `reason` says why. A
provider's address and key are never shown, and nothing here asks a provider whether it
answers: a turn that cannot reach it ends with an `error` event.

200.description: The chat's availability in the team

post.description:
A person in a browser session, any member of the team: a token is `403 session_required` —
an agent with a token has the MCP server (docs/adr/0040) — and the CSRF check holds as for
every write of a session (docs/adr/0037). A team without the chat is `409
chat_unavailable`, and `GET …/chat` says why; a `provider` the installation does not configure
is `400 validation_failed`. A person with as many turns running as
`COWORK_CHAT_TURNS_PER_PERSON` allows on the replica — in another tab, say — is `429
chat_busy`. The backend keeps nothing between turns: the request carries the conversation,
and the answer the messages to append to it.

A turn runs the provider's model and the tools it calls: at most `COWORK_CHAT_MAX_STEPS` calls
of the model, for at most `COWORK_CHAT_TURN_TIMEOUT`. Every tool call is a request of this API
with the person's session, marked as the agent `chat/<model>/<conversation>`
(docs/adr/0036): it holds the capabilities the person chose for the chat (`GET
/api/v1/me/chat`, docs/adr/0043 D5), passes validation, authorization, the agent rules and the
audit like any agent's request, and what it changes reaches the event stream. It runs at once:
nothing waits for the person. It works in the turn's team only. A tool the API refuses — an
act that needs a capability the person did not give the chat is `403 agent_forbidden`
naming it — is an answer the model reads, not a failed turn. A call's creating requests carry
keys derived from the conversation and the call; a turn the model answers anew repeats its
acts: a client never retries one by itself.

The answer is `200` with `text/event-stream`, each event an `event:` line with its name and
a `data:` line with its JSON, flushed one by one:

- `text` — `ChatTextEvent`: the next piece of the assistant's text.
- `tool_call` — `ChatToolCall`: a call the model made, with its arguments, before it runs.
- `ui` — `ChatUiEvent`: between a call of `open_ticket`, `open_backlog` or `open_board` and its
  result, the page of this UI the client shows next.
- `tool_result` — `ChatToolResultEvent`: whether the call succeeded, and the start of what it
  answered the model.
- `error` — `Problem`: why the turn failed once it had begun — `chat_provider_failed`,
  `timeout` (`COWORK_CHAT_TURN_TIMEOUT`), `not_ready` (the server is shutting down: send
  the turn again), `internal`.
- `done` — `ChatDoneEvent`, always the last: the messages the turn added, to be appended to
  the conversation as they are, and why the turn ended — `stopped` when
  `DELETE …/chat/turns` ended it.

A `: keep-alive` comment follows ten seconds without an event, so no proxy closes a turn
while the model thinks. A stream that ends without `done` was cut — the network, the client's
abort, a shutdown —, and the acts its `tool_result` events reported have happened. A call
the turn's end left without an answer is answered to the model on the next turn as one
that did not run. An answer of the model that is white space only adds no message: `done`
carries none for it.

**Limits.** A body above `COWORK_MAX_JSON_BODY` is `413 payload_too_large`; more messages or
longer texts than `ChatTurn` allows are `400 validation_failed` — the conversation is too
long, and a new one begins. A message the model could not read in its place — a tool
message that answers no call, a conversation that does not end with the person's message —
is `400 validation_failed` naming it.
post.summary: One turn of the chat, answered as server-sent events

delete.description:
A person in a browser session, any member: a token is `403 session_required`, a session the
agent header marks `403 agent_forbidden`, and the CSRF check holds. Every turn of the
session's person in the team that runs on the replica answering this request ends at once:
its call of the model is cancelled, so is a tool call in flight, and its stream ends with
`done` and the reason `stopped`. The answer comes once those turns have ended, or after five
seconds; a turn of another person, or of the person in another team, runs on. What the
stopped turns' tool calls did before has happened.

The turns are those of this replica (docs/adr/0076): behind several backend replicas a turn
another replica runs is not reached — the client's abort of the turn's own request still is.
With no turn running, nothing happens, and the answer is the same.

delete.summary: Stop every running turn of the person in the team

`read` scope, any member. The tiles of docs/adr/0018 D6 — open tickets by state, by
severity, the open `live` and `boundary` findings, the blocked tickets, the age of the open
tickets, throughput, lead time, open decisions and the time booked — and, beside them, the
open tickets updated last. Each tile is defined in its field of `Dashboard`, and each counts
only what the caller can see.

The filters are the ticket lists' `project` (docs/adr/0049 D6), repeatable, `!` leaving a
project out, and the period, `from` and `to`, both days inclusive — by default the thirty
days that end today (UTC); `from` after `to` is `400 validation_failed`. The period bounds
the time booked; throughput and lead time end with its last day; the open tiles stand as
the tickets do at the request.

One route for all nine: the page shows them together under one set of filters, one
transaction gives counts that agree with each other, and a reload after an event costs one
request, which `If-None-Match` answers with `304` while nothing the caller sees changed
(docs/adr/0054 D7). A token restricted to a project does not reach it.

each with who deleted it and when the purge job removes it (docs/adr/0024 D1, D2): the one

restricted to a project is refused like an unknown team.

delete.description:
A team administrator's act, never an agent's (docs/adr/0024 D2, D7, docs/adr/0043 D3),
**in a browser session only**: the one irreversible act on a ticket, so a token — an
administrator's `admin` token included — answers `403 session_required`, and the purge job
does the rest thirty days after the deletion (docs/adr/0024 D7 as amended 2026-10-05). On a
ticket of the bin only — any other key is 404. The ticket, its
comments, questions, links, stakes, time entries, notifications and attachments are removed,
and the attachments' objects after them; its children become roots, and a block that waited
on it waits on its key as an external reference. Its audit rows stay with their content
emptied: the key, the actor and the act remain (docs/adr/0026 D3). The key stays taken.
Irreversible: the browser asks a second time. Recorded as `purged` and published.

docs/adr/0043 D3), on a ticket of the bin only — any other key is 404. The ticket comes back
as it was, its links, comments and place in the rank with it; the version rises. Recorded as
`restored` and published.

get.description:
`ticket.changed` (an upload included), `comment.changed`, `question.changed`,
`link.changed` and `interest.changed`, each with `data: {"key", "version", "kind"}` — a key
and a version, never content (docs/adr/0054 D2); `id:` is the act's id. An event of a
project the caller cannot see, or of a confidential ticket they may not read, never
arrives (D3).

`ticket.changed` of `kind` `derived` says that a parent's derived stages moved because a
child of another team changed (docs/adr/0017 D3 as amended 2026-10-10); it is sent on the
parent's team's streams, under the same rules, and the client reloads the ticket. The change
is no act, so its `id:` is made for the event and names no act.

`project.changed` says that a project's tickets changed as a whole — its rank set by the
score (docs/adr/0014 D3), `kind` `ranked`, or an import executed into it (docs/adr/0051 D3),
`kind` `imported`, whose tickets announce no event of their own — with
`data: {"key": "<team>/<PROJECT>", "kind": …}`; `id:` is the act's id. It reaches whoever
sees the project, and the client reloads the lists it shows.

`membership.changed` says that who belongs to the team, or who sees a project, changed —
by an administrator's act or by the identity provider's groups (docs/adr/0030 D2, D6). Its
`data` carries the team's slug, `team` — and the same slug under the deprecated `tenant`,
written for one release and dropped in a later one (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7) —,
and keys only, each where it applies:
`person_id`, the person whose membership or project access changed; `project_id`, the
project whose restriction or access list changed; `mapping_id`, the group mapping made,
changed or removed. The client reloads what it shows of that team's members, mappings and
access lists, its project list when `project_id` is there, and the person's own
`GET /api/v1/me`. An event about an access entry reaches the team's administrators and the
person it names, one about a mapping the administrators, every other every member.

With `me=true` — the person-level pages, and the bell in the top bar — the stream carries
every event of every team the person belongs to that the team's own stream would carry
to them, each with its `id:` (docs/adr/0054 D1, D3), and `inbox.changed` with
`data: {"unread": n}`, the person's unread notifications in every team the request reaches
(`GET /api/v1/me/inbox` counts the same), sent when the stream opens and whenever the inbox
changes — a notification for them, or theirs marked read. The count carries no `id:` and is
not replayed: it says how things stand. A team the person is granted a role in is followed
at once, one they leave no more after the act that took it away. A token restricted to a
team hears its team alone (docs/adr/0035 D3).

A reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` inside the replay window replays the gap — on a person-level
stream the gap of every team it follows, in the order the server received the events;
beyond it the stream starts with `event: resync`, and the client refetches its lists (D5).
A comment every twenty seconds keeps proxies open and checks the token and the
memberships again; the stream ends when the token or the membership of the team in the
path fails. `event: unavailable` ends a stream
the server closes — the person's eleventh, a shutdown — and the client polls (D7, D8).

(docs/adr/0043 D3), so an agent's request is 403 `agent_forbidden`, `hard-off: deleting,
restoring or purging`, before the filter is looked at. A team administrator deletes another
person's shared filter — one whose owner left the team among them —, an administration act
with `admin` scope (docs/adr/0018 D5): a token with less than `admin` scope is 403

with less than `admin` scope 403 `insufficient_scope`, an agent 403 `agent_forbidden`; the
filter answered is one the administrator no longer reads. Another person's shared filter is

with the fields that changed.

Each mapping gives its role to every person whose groups include its
group; several matches yield the highest role (docs/adr/0030 D2).
`includes_caller` says the calling person is one of them, so the editor
can warn before a change takes the editor's own role away. The team's
administrators read them, and a global administrator who holds no role
in the team, in a browser session (docs/adr/0034 D2).

post.description:
The group is matched exactly, case and all, against the groups the
identity provider's claim carries (docs/adr/0029 D2). The mapping applies
at once to every person whose groups, as of their last login or groups
refresh, include it: their memberships are derived in the same
transaction, recorded with the cause `mapping`. Everyone else is caught
up at their next login or groups refresh (docs/adr/0030 D5). A group the
team maps already is `409 mapping_exists`.

Only a global administrator who administers the team maps a group, in
a browser session; any other administrator of the team is
`403 forbidden`, and nothing is written. Every team shares the identity
provider's one namespace of groups, and a mapping admits everyone in its
group at once (docs/adr/0030 D7).

administrator of the team may remove one, with an `admin`-scope token

exists: who has logged in through the identity provider once, or has a

`404 person_not_found`; an address several persons share is
`409 person_ambiguous`, since an e-mail address is a display attribute
and not an identity (docs/adr/0029 D5); a person who holds a grant here
already is `409 grant_exists` — change it with

added by e-mail address or username.

A global administrator who does not hold `admin` in the team — who
holds no role there, or a lower one — sets their own grant here, their
own id as `person_id` and any role (docs/adr/0034 D2): a marked grant like
any other, made or its role changed under the team's lock, recorded in
the team's audit with the administrator as its actor and announced to
its members as `membership.changed`. It takes no administrator away, so
it is never `409 last_admin`; it is how a team left without an
administrator who can log in gets one again. A grant to anybody else
stays an administrator's act: `403 forbidden`.

an agent too (docs/adr/0051 D6, docs/adr/0064 D5); a restricted project the caller cannot see
is `404`. Every export is recorded, one act `exported` on the project — data left the system
(docs/adr/0059 D3, docs/adr/0026 D5) —, and never published. A recorded read: a session's

The first phase of an import (docs/adr/0051 D1, D2): every file of the upload is read, and the
answer is the new job, a dry run whose report says per file what the execution would do.
Nothing is imported yet. The upload is `multipart/form-data` with one or more parts named
`file`: one archive — a `tar.gz` or a `zip`, known by its bytes, not its name — or Markdown
files, one per part, named by the part's file name.

A file is read as a ticket file of a repository (`NNN-<slug>.md`, `local_NNN-<slug>.md`,
docs/adr/0063 D3), as cowork's own export (`<PROJECT>-<n>.md`, grammar v1), or, without
frontmatter, as an archived record that becomes one done task (D4); everything else is listed
as skipped (D5), and so is a `/context` document, with its reason (docs/adr/0044 D3); the
manifests of an export — `manifest.json`, `links.json`, `attachments.json` — are read beside
the tickets. The numbers are kept (docs/adr/0007 D6): a number that is a ticket of the project
already, a deleted one included, is a conflict (docs/adr/0064 D3), and one a purged ticket held
is given back, with a warning (docs/adr/0007 D4); the type is detected by content and open to
correction (docs/adr/0008 D5); `blocked` is never inferred (docs/adr/0009); a value outside its
vocabulary is an error, never a guess (docs/adr/0010 D5); the confidential flag follows the
rule of the source (docs/adr/0065 D7); no parent is guessed — a file names its own, or the
person or their agent sets it after the import (docs/adr/0051 D2).

A writer's act of the project, as creating a ticket is: the role `member` in the team — a
restricted project's list may lower it — and a token's `write` scope; an agent's too
(docs/adr/0051 D6, docs/adr/0043 D2). An import through a token, an agent's or not, assigns a
confidential ticket to the token's own person or to nobody, the report saying why on the file
(docs/adr/0065 D9, docs/adr/0043 D3); a browser session's assigns as the file says. A body above `COWORK_MAX_IMPORT_BYTES` and 64 KiB of multipart
overhead is `413 payload_too_large`, and so are files that hold more than
`COWORK_MAX_IMPORT_BYTES` unpacked, or more than 10 000 files — a `zip`'s entries counted, its
directories included, before it is read (docs/adr/0051 D7); an archived project is `409
project_archived`. Recorded as the act `created` on the `import_job`; the dry run is kept for
twenty-four hours, after which its read and its execution answer `404`.

like a missing one everywhere but the team's bin (`GET …/deleted-tickets`) — every route of

(docs/adr/0024 D1, D3). Its parent's derived stages leave it out. Recorded as `deleted` and

patch.description:
`If-Match` is required (docs/adr/0050 D3). Assigning a confidential ticket admits the new
assignee (docs/adr/0065 D9): an agent assigns a confidential ticket — or one the change
makes confidential — only to its own person or to nobody, and another new assignee is 403
`agent_forbidden` (docs/adr/0043 D3); a person's token is held the same way, and another
new assignee is 403 `session_required` — admitting a person takes a browser session
(docs/adr/0035 D5).

The three progress stages — `progress_refinement`, `progress` (implementation),
`progress_review` — take 0 to 100 in steps of five in every state but dropped, and not on a
ticket with children, whose stages are derived (409 `state_conflict`; docs/adr/0017 D2, D3).
A change that brings the last of the three to 100 on a ticket without children is the done act
in the same transaction (docs/adr/0009 D5, docs/adr/0017 D4): it needs `note`, the
verification (400 at `/note` otherwise); over open prerequisites it is 409
`open_prerequisites` unless a person sends `override_prerequisites` with a `reason`; an agent
needs `close` and a ticket in in-progress or review (403 `agent_forbidden`) and never
overrides. The ticket is then done by its stages: `done_by_hand` false, `done_from` the state
it left, its rank taken away; a `transitioned` act carries the note beside the `updated` act.
A change that lowers a stage of a ticket done by its stages reopens it to `done_from`, with a
`reason` (400 at `/reason` otherwise), ranked at the bottom of its project. A ticket done by
hand keeps its state while its stages change. `note`, `override_prerequisites` and `reason`
on a change that moves no state are 400. The version rises once.

For every member of the team. The chat is available when the installation configures at

the first being the one a turn uses when it names none. Otherwise `reason` says why. A
provider's address and key are never shown, and nothing here asks a provider whether it
answers: a turn that cannot reach it ends with an `error` event.

post.description:
Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/chat`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

A person in a browser session, any member of the team: a token is `403 session_required` —
an agent with a token has the MCP server (docs/adr/0040) — and the CSRF check holds as for
every write of a session (docs/adr/0037). A team without the chat is `409
chat_unavailable`, and `GET …/chat` says why; a `provider` the installation does not configure
is `400 validation_failed`. A person with as many turns running as
`COWORK_CHAT_TURNS_PER_PERSON` allows on the replica — in another tab, say — is `429
chat_busy`. The backend keeps nothing between turns: the request carries the conversation,
and the answer the messages to append to it.

A turn runs the provider's model and the tools it calls: at most `COWORK_CHAT_MAX_STEPS` calls
of the model, for at most `COWORK_CHAT_TURN_TIMEOUT`. Every tool call is a request of this API
with the person's session, marked as the agent `chat/<model>/<conversation>`
(docs/adr/0036): it holds the capabilities the person chose for the chat (`GET
/api/v1/me/chat`, docs/adr/0043 D5), passes validation, authorization, the agent rules and the
audit like any agent's request, and what it changes reaches the event stream. It runs at once:
nothing waits for the person. It works in the turn's team only. A tool the API refuses — an
act that needs a capability the person did not give the chat is `403 agent_forbidden`
naming it — is an answer the model reads, not a failed turn. A call's creating requests carry
keys derived from the conversation and the call; a turn the model answers anew repeats its
acts: a client never retries one by itself.

The answer is `200` with `text/event-stream`, each event an `event:` line with its name and
a `data:` line with its JSON, flushed one by one:

- `text` — `ChatTextEvent`: the next piece of the assistant's text.
- `tool_call` — `ChatToolCall`: a call the model made, with its arguments, before it runs.
- `ui` — `ChatUiEvent`: between a call of `open_ticket`, `open_backlog` or `open_board` and its
  result, the page of this UI the client shows next.
- `tool_result` — `ChatToolResultEvent`: whether the call succeeded, and the start of what it
  answered the model.
- `error` — `Problem`: why the turn failed once it had begun — `chat_provider_failed`,
  `timeout` (`COWORK_CHAT_TURN_TIMEOUT`), `not_ready` (the server is shutting down: send
  the turn again), `internal`.
- `done` — `ChatDoneEvent`, always the last: the messages the turn added, to be appended to
  the conversation as they are, and why the turn ended — `stopped` when
  `DELETE …/chat/turns` ended it.

A `: keep-alive` comment follows ten seconds without an event, so no proxy closes a turn
while the model thinks. A stream that ends without `done` was cut — the network, the client's
abort, a shutdown —, and the acts its `tool_result` events reported have happened. A call
the turn's end left without an answer is answered to the model on the next turn as one
that did not run. An answer of the model that is white space only adds no message: `done`
carries none for it.

**Limits.** A body above `COWORK_MAX_JSON_BODY` is `413 payload_too_large`; more messages or
longer texts than `ChatTurn` allows are `400 validation_failed` — the conversation is too
long, and a new one begins. A message the model could not read in its place — a tool
message that answers no call, a conversation that does not end with the person's message —
is `400 validation_failed` naming it.
post.summary: Deprecated: One turn of the chat, answered as server-sent events

delete.description:
Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/chat/turns`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

A person in a browser session, any member: a token is `403 session_required`, a session the
agent header marks `403 agent_forbidden`, and the CSRF check holds. Every turn of the
session's person in the team that runs on the replica answering this request ends at once:
its call of the model is cancelled, so is a tool call in flight, and its stream ends with
`done` and the reason `stopped`. The answer comes once those turns have ended, or after five
seconds; a turn of another person, or of the person in another team, runs on. What the
stopped turns' tool calls did before has happened.

The turns are those of this replica (docs/adr/0076): behind several backend replicas a turn
another replica runs is not reached — the client's abort of the turn's own request still is.
With no turn running, nothing happens, and the answer is the same.

204.description: The person's turns in the team on this replica are stopped

get.description:
Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/dashboard`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

`read` scope, any member. The tiles of docs/adr/0018 D6 — open tickets by state, by
severity, the open `live` and `boundary` findings, the blocked tickets, the age of the open
tickets, throughput, lead time, open decisions and the time booked — and, beside them, the
open tickets updated last. Each tile is defined in its field of `Dashboard`, and each counts
only what the caller can see.

The filters are the ticket lists' `project` (docs/adr/0049 D6), repeatable, `!` leaving a
project out, and the period, `from` and `to`, both days inclusive — by default the thirty
days that end today (UTC); `from` after `to` is `400 validation_failed`. The period bounds
the time booked; throughput and lead time end with its last day; the open tiles stand as
the tickets do at the request.

One route for all nine: the page shows them together under one set of filters, one
transaction gives counts that agree with each other, and a reload after an event costs one
request, which `If-None-Match` answers with `304` while nothing the caller sees changed
(docs/adr/0054 D7). A token restricted to a project does not reach it.
get.summary: Deprecated: The team's dashboard, its nine tiles over what the caller can see

The team administrators' view of the deleted tickets they can see, the last deleted first,
each with who deleted it and when the purge job removes it (docs/adr/0024 D1, D2): the one
list in which a deleted ticket exists. An administrator's, with `read` scope; a token

delete.description:
Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/deleted-tickets/{key}`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

A team administrator's act, never an agent's (docs/adr/0024 D2, D7, docs/adr/0043 D3),
**in a browser session only**: the one irreversible act on a ticket, so a token — an
administrator's `admin` token included — answers `403 session_required`, and the purge job
does the rest thirty days after the deletion (docs/adr/0024 D7 as amended 2026-10-05). On a
ticket of the bin only — any other key is 404. The ticket, its
comments, questions, links, stakes, time entries, notifications and attachments are removed,
and the attachments' objects after them; its children become roots, and a block that waited
on it waits on its key as an external reference. Its audit rows stay with their content
emptied: the key, the actor and the act remain (docs/adr/0026 D3). The key stays taken.
Irreversible: the browser asks a second time. Recorded as `purged` and published.

A team administrator's act with `admin` scope, never an agent's (docs/adr/0024 D1, D7,
docs/adr/0043 D3), on a ticket of the bin only — any other key is 404. The ticket comes back
as it was, its links, comments and place in the rank with it; the version rises. Recorded as
`restored` and published.

get.description:
Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/events`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

`ticket.changed` (an upload included), `comment.changed`, `question.changed`,
`link.changed` and `interest.changed`, each with `data: {"key", "version", "kind"}` — a key
and a version, never content (docs/adr/0054 D2); `id:` is the act's id. An event of a
project the caller cannot see, or of a confidential ticket they may not read, never
arrives (D3).

`ticket.changed` of `kind` `derived` says that a parent's derived stages moved because a
child of another team changed (docs/adr/0017 D3 as amended 2026-10-10); it is sent on the
parent's team's streams, under the same rules, and the client reloads the ticket. The change
is no act, so its `id:` is made for the event and names no act.

`project.changed` says that a project's tickets changed as a whole — its rank set by the
score (docs/adr/0014 D3), `kind` `ranked`, or an import executed into it (docs/adr/0051 D3),
`kind` `imported`, whose tickets announce no event of their own — with
`data: {"key": "<team>/<PROJECT>", "kind": …}`; `id:` is the act's id. It reaches whoever
sees the project, and the client reloads the lists it shows.

`membership.changed` says that who belongs to the team, or who sees a project, changed —
by an administrator's act or by the identity provider's groups (docs/adr/0030 D2, D6). Its
`data` carries the team's slug, `team` — and the same slug under the deprecated `tenant`,
written for one release and dropped in a later one (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7) —,
and keys only, each where it applies:
`person_id`, the person whose membership or project access changed; `project_id`, the
project whose restriction or access list changed; `mapping_id`, the group mapping made,
changed or removed. The client reloads what it shows of that team's members, mappings and
access lists, its project list when `project_id` is there, and the person's own
`GET /api/v1/me`. An event about an access entry reaches the team's administrators and the
person it names, one about a mapping the administrators, every other every member.

With `me=true` — the person-level pages, and the bell in the top bar — the stream carries
every event of every team the person belongs to that the team's own stream would carry
to them, each with its `id:` (docs/adr/0054 D1, D3), and `inbox.changed` with
`data: {"unread": n}`, the person's unread notifications in every team the request reaches
(`GET /api/v1/me/inbox` counts the same), sent when the stream opens and whenever the inbox
changes — a notification for them, or theirs marked read. The count carries no `id:` and is
not replayed: it says how things stand. A team the person is granted a role in is followed
at once, one they leave no more after the act that took it away. A token restricted to a
team hears its team alone (docs/adr/0035 D3).

A reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` inside the replay window replays the gap — on a person-level
stream the gap of every team it follows, in the order the server received the events;
beyond it the stream starts with `event: resync`, and the client refetches its lists (D5).
A comment every twenty seconds keeps proxies open and checks the token and the
memberships again; the stream ends when the token or the membership of the team in the
path fails. `event: unavailable` ends a stream
the server closes — the person's eleventh, a shutdown — and the client polls (D7, D8).

count; the confidential tickets left out are counted per project and in total. Any member, an
agent too; a token restricted to a project is refused, as on every route of the team outside
a project. One act `exported` on the team, never published. A recorded read: a session's
request with `Sec-Fetch-Site` `same-site` or `cross-site` is `403 csrf` (docs/adr/0026 D5).

The caller's own filters and every filter a member shared with the team, oldest first, each
with its owner. Every filter is checked against the vocabularies as it is read
(docs/adr/0049 D7): a value that no longer validates is in `warnings`. A filter of somebody
else that names a project or a ticket the caller cannot see — or one that no longer exists —
is answered `redacted`, without its parameters, as an act that names a hidden ticket is
(docs/adr/0065 D5). A token restricted to a project is refused like an unknown team.

(docs/adr/0049 D1) and are refused as the lists refuse them — an unknown parameter or a value
outside its vocabulary is 400 at `/parameters/<name>` (D4). `me` stays `me`: whoever applies
the filter is meant. `shared` shows it to every member of the team with the owner beside
it. Recorded as `created`.

Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/filters/{filter}`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

Its owner's act with `write` scope, and never an agent's: a deletion is on the hard-off list
(docs/adr/0043 D3), so an agent's request is 403 `agent_forbidden`, `hard-off: deleting,
restoring or purging`, before the filter is looked at. A team administrator deletes another
person's shared filter — one whose owner left the team among them —, an administration act
with `admin` scope (docs/adr/0018 D5): a token with less than `admin` scope is 403
`insufficient_scope`. Another person's shared filter is 403 `forbidden` to everyone else, a
filter the caller cannot see — or one already gone, or no longer shared — 404. Recorded as
`deleted`.

Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/filters/{filter}`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

Its owner's act with `write` scope and `If-Match` (docs/adr/0050 D3); `parameters` replaces
the whole set, checked as on creation. A team administrator unshares another person's
shared filter — one whose owner left the team among them — with `{"shared": false}` and
nothing else, an administration act with `admin` scope that no agent makes
(docs/adr/0018 D5, docs/adr/0043 D3): any other change of it is 403 `forbidden`, a token
with less than `admin` scope 403 `insufficient_scope`, an agent 403 `agent_forbidden`; the
filter answered is one the administrator no longer reads. Another person's shared filter is
403 `forbidden` to everyone else, a filter the caller cannot see 404. Recorded as `updated`
with the fields that changed.

get.description:
Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/group-mappings`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

Each mapping gives its role to every person whose groups include its
group; several matches yield the highest role (docs/adr/0030 D2).
`includes_caller` says the calling person is one of them, so the editor
can warn before a change takes the editor's own role away. The team's
administrators read them, and a global administrator who holds no role
in the team, in a browser session (docs/adr/0034 D2).
get.summary: Deprecated: The team's group mappings, by group

post.description:
Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/group-mappings`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

The group is matched exactly, case and all, against the groups the
identity provider's claim carries (docs/adr/0029 D2). The mapping applies
at once to every person whose groups, as of their last login or groups
refresh, include it: their memberships are derived in the same
transaction, recorded with the cause `mapping`. Everyone else is caught
up at their next login or groups refresh (docs/adr/0030 D5). A group the
team maps already is `409 mapping_exists`.

Only a global administrator who administers the team maps a group, in
a browser session; any other administrator of the team is
`403 forbidden`, and nothing is written. Every team shares the identity
provider's one namespace of groups, and a mapping admits everyone in its
group at once (docs/adr/0030 D7).

The memberships it derived go at once, or fall to the highest of the
person's other mapped groups; grants stay (docs/adr/0030 D3). Any
administrator of the team may remove one, with an `admin`-scope token

Idempotent: removing a mapping that does not exist answers 204 as well.

derives change at once, as at its creation. Like its creation, a global
administrator's who administers the team: any other administrator is

Each member with the effective role — the higher of the mapped and the
granted one (docs/adr/0030 D4) — and `origins`, every source with its
own role; `local` marks a person with a local account rather than an
identity of the identity provider (docs/adr/0033). `email` is the
address that tells two persons of one name apart, for the team's
administrators; everyone else reads null — a global administrator who
holds no role in the team and reads the list as part of its
administration too (docs/adr/0034 D2). Paged by cursor, or by number
with a total (docs/adr/0048 D2).

A manual grant, marked as such (docs/adr/0030 D3), for a person who
exists: who has logged in through the identity provider once, or has a
local account. Nobody active by that address or name is
`404 person_not_found`; an address several persons share is
`409 person_ambiguous`, since an e-mail address is a display attribute
and not an identity (docs/adr/0029 D5); a person who holds a grant here
already is `409 grant_exists` — change it with
`PUT …/members/{person_id}/grant`. A person with a mapped membership gets
the grant beside it, and the higher role of the two applies (D4).

put.description:
Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/members/{person_id}/grant`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

Creates the member's manual grant with the role, or changes the role of
the one they hold; repeating it changes nothing (docs/adr/0045 D1). The
mapped membership is never touched: it holds until the mapping or the
groups change (docs/adr/0030 D3). The person must be a member of the
team, else `404 person_not_found` — a person who is not one yet is
added by e-mail address or username.

A global administrator who does not hold `admin` in the team — who
holds no role there, or a lower one — sets their own grant here, their
own id as `person_id` and any role (docs/adr/0034 D2): a marked grant like
any other, made or its role changed under the team's lock, recorded in
the team's audit with the administrator as its actor and announced to
its members as `membership.changed`. It takes no administrator away, so
it is never `409 last_admin`; it is how a team left without an
administrator who can log in gets one again. A grant to anybody else
stays an administrator's act: `403 forbidden`.

Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/projects/{project}/export`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

A `tar.gz` (docs/adr/0051 D4) with, for every ticket of the project the caller can see — done
and dropped ones included, deleted ones not —, its `…/markdown` document named by its key,
`<team>/<PROJECT>-<n>.md`; and three manifests at the root:

- `manifest.json`, an `ExportManifest`: the format, the team, the project with its count of
  tickets, the time, the exporter, and the confidential tickets the caller cannot see and the
  archive therefore leaves out, as a count (docs/adr/0065 D5);
- `links.json`, an array of `ExportLink`: every link with an end in the project whose two ends
  the caller can see, once, by its source key, its type and its target key;
- `attachments.json`, an array of `ExportAttachment`: every attachment of those tickets by its
  ticket, name, type, size and URL — never its bytes (docs/adr/0016 D5).

The importer reads the archive back (docs/adr/0051 D5). Whoever reads the project exports it,
an agent too (docs/adr/0051 D6, docs/adr/0064 D5); a restricted project the caller cannot see
is `404`. Every export is recorded, one act `exported` on the project — data left the system
(docs/adr/0059 D3, docs/adr/0026 D5) —, and never published. A recorded read: a session's
request with `Sec-Fetch-Site` `same-site` or `cross-site` is `403 csrf`.

post.description:
Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/projects/{project}/imports`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

The first phase of an import (docs/adr/0051 D1, D2): every file of the upload is read, and the
answer is the new job, a dry run whose report says per file what the execution would do.
Nothing is imported yet. The upload is `multipart/form-data` with one or more parts named
`file`: one archive — a `tar.gz` or a `zip`, known by its bytes, not its name — or Markdown
files, one per part, named by the part's file name.

A file is read as a ticket file of a repository (`NNN-<slug>.md`, `local_NNN-<slug>.md`,
docs/adr/0063 D3), as cowork's own export (`<PROJECT>-<n>.md`, grammar v1), or, without
frontmatter, as an archived record that becomes one done task (D4); everything else is listed
as skipped (D5), and so is a `/context` document, with its reason (docs/adr/0044 D3); the
manifests of an export — `manifest.json`, `links.json`, `attachments.json` — are read beside
the tickets. The numbers are kept (docs/adr/0007 D6): a number that is a ticket of the project
already, a deleted one included, is a conflict (docs/adr/0064 D3), and one a purged ticket held
is given back, with a warning (docs/adr/0007 D4); the type is detected by content and open to
correction (docs/adr/0008 D5); `blocked` is never inferred (docs/adr/0009); a value outside its
vocabulary is an error, never a guess (docs/adr/0010 D5); the confidential flag follows the
rule of the source (docs/adr/0065 D7); no parent is guessed — a file names its own, or the
person or their agent sets it after the import (docs/adr/0051 D2).

A writer's act of the project, as creating a ticket is: the role `member` in the team — a
restricted project's list may lower it — and a token's `write` scope; an agent's too
(docs/adr/0051 D6, docs/adr/0043 D2). An import through a token, an agent's or not, assigns a
confidential ticket to the token's own person or to nobody, the report saying why on the file
(docs/adr/0065 D9, docs/adr/0043 D3); a browser session's assigns as the file says. A body above `COWORK_MAX_IMPORT_BYTES` and 64 KiB of multipart
overhead is `413 payload_too_large`, and so are files that hold more than
`COWORK_MAX_IMPORT_BYTES` unpacked, or more than 10 000 files — a `zip`'s entries counted, its
directories included, before it is read (docs/adr/0051 D7); an archived project is `409
project_archived`. Recorded as the act `created` on the `import_job`; the dry run is kept for
twenty-four hours, after which its read and its execution answer `404`.

post.description:
Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/projects/{project}/imports/{import}/execution`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

The second phase (docs/adr/0051 D2, D3): the dry run's files are read again with the
corrections — a file left out, a type, a state, an assignee (docs/adr/0063 D1, docs/adr/0008
D5) — against the project as it stands now, and every ticket, question and link is created in
one transaction, the project's sequence advanced past the highest number, or nothing is. The
tickets keep their numbers and take their places at the bottom of the project's rank in number
order; the importer is their reporter; the dates, the stages, the horizon and the block are the
source's, and a ticket imported as done or dropped carries its note or reason on its act
(docs/adr/0063 D2). Every ticket records the file it came from and the job.

Each created row is an act of the importer naming the job: `created` on each ticket, with
`confidential_set` where the flag is set, `transitioned` for a done or dropped ticket, `asked`
on each question, `linked` on both ends of each link; and `imported` on the job. The event
streams hear one `project.changed` with the kind `imported`, not an event per ticket, and
nobody's inbox is told.

The execution imports every file it can and leaves out each file with an error or a conflict —
one whose number a ticket filed since the dry run holds included —, its `reason` saying why
(docs/adr/0051 D2, docs/adr/0064 D3); nothing refuses it but a second execution. An assignee is
the member the dry run named: a file's identity that resolves to anybody else by now assigns
nobody, with a warning. A dry run is executed at most once: a second execution is `409
import_executed`. A correction naming no file of the job, or breaking the rules of
`ImportCorrection`, is `400` at its pointer. The same writers as the dry run, of their own dry
runs, and the team's administrators: another person's dry run is `404`; an archived project
is `409 project_archived`; a dry run older than twenty-four hours is `404`.

and records nothing. Never automatic. A member's act with `write` scope; an agent
needs `rank` (docs/adr/0043 D4). No `If-Match`: it names the order, not a state it overwrites

A member's act with `write` scope, in the agent baseline (docs/adr/0043 D2). The number is
the project's next. `horizon` is the ticket's horizon, a planning category independent of
the state, `later` when left out; another horizon is the ticket's set horizon, set by the
caller and without a reason (docs/adr/0010 D3). The ticket joins the rank at the bottom,

`set-horizon` for a horizon other than `later` and `rank` for a place, else 403
`agent_forbidden` (docs/adr/0043 D4). A live or boundary security class makes the ticket
confidential (docs/adr/0065 D2); an agent assigns a confidential filing only to its own
person, else 403 `agent_forbidden` (docs/adr/0043 D3), and so does a person's token, else
403 `session_required` — admitting another person takes a browser session
(docs/adr/0035 D5). An archived project refuses.

A team administrator's act with `admin` scope, never an agent's (docs/adr/0024 D7,
docs/adr/0043 D3; 403 `agent_forbidden`). The ticket is soft-deleted: from then on it answers
like a missing one everywhere but the team's bin (`GET …/deleted-tickets`) — every route of
it and under it is 404, and it leaves every list, the prerequisite trees, the person-level
lists, the inbox and the context; links to it are hidden, not removed, and its key stays taken
(docs/adr/0024 D1, D3). Its parent's derived stages leave it out. Recorded as `deleted` and
published. A restoration brings everything back; thirty days after the deletion the purge job
removes it for good (D2). Deleting a ticket that others depend on is not refused — the browser
shows the dependents and asks first (D7).

patch.description:
Deprecated: `/api/v1/teams/{team}/projects/{project}/tickets/{number}`, served under the name before for one release and removed in a later one, answering as it does (docs/adr/0005 D1, docs/adr/0046 D7).

`If-Match` is required (docs/adr/0050 D3). Assigning a confidential ticket admits the new
assignee (docs/adr/0065 D9): an agent assigns a confidential ticket — or one the change
makes confidential — only to its own person or to nobody, and another new assignee is 403
`agent_forbidden` (docs/adr/0043 D3); a person's token is held the same way, and another
new assignee is 403 `session_required` — admitting a person takes a browser session
(docs/adr/0035 D5).

The three progress stages — `progress_refinement`, `progress` (implementation),
`progress_review` — take 0 to 100 in steps of five in every state but dropped, and not on a
ticket with children, whose stages are derived (409 `state_conflict`; docs/adr/0017 D2, D3).
A change that brings the last of the three to 100 on a ticket without children is the done act
in the same transaction (docs/adr/0009 D5, docs/adr/0017 D4): it needs `note`, the
verification (400 at `/note` otherwise); over open prerequisites it is 409
`open_prerequisites` unless a person sends `override_prerequisites` with a `reason`; an agent
needs `close` and a ticket in in-progress or review (403 `agent_forbidden`) and never
overrides. The ticket is then done by its stages: `done_by_hand` false, `done_from` the state
it left, its rank taken away; a `transitioned` act carries the note beside the `updated` act.
A change that lowers a stage of a ticket done by its stages reopens it to `done_from`, with a
`reason` (400 at `/reason` otherwise), ranked at the bottom of its project. A ticket done by
hand keeps its state while its stages change. `note`, `override_prerequisites` and `reason`
on a change that moves no state are 400. The version rises once.

is work no list needs. The HTML is rendered and sanitised on the server: raw HTML is shown
as text; a link keeps only an `http`, `https` or `mailto` address or one relative to the

own path (docs/adr/0016 D7), and any other image is a link to its address. Shown through
Angular's own sanitiser, never trusted past it. The `ETag` is the ticket's, the one a
replacement of the body names in `If-Match`; the HTML changes with the ticket's
attachments as well, which raise no version.

title above the body above comments, questions and file names, a title found by trigram
below them (D4). A hit names the ticket — its key, title, type and state —, where it matched
(`found_in`: the key, the ticket's own text, a comment by its id, a question by its number, an
attachment's name) and a snippet of that text with the matched words marked (`ts_headline`,
D5). The snippet is text in parts, never HTML: a client shows every part as text.

Only what the caller can see is searched, snippets included: a restricted project they are
not on, a confidential ticket of which they are neither a team administrator, the assignee
nor the reporter, and a project-restricted token's other projects find nothing
(docs/adr/0034 D3, docs/adr/0065 D5). Cursor paging only, no total (docs/adr/0048 D3); a
cursor belongs to its query.

The `q` filter of the ticket lists is not this search: it narrows a list to the tickets whose
title and body hold every word, in the list's own order, with no rank and no snippet.

get.description:
Where the issuer sends the browser back: `COWORK_BASE_URL` +
`/auth/callback`, the redirect URI registered with the identity
provider (docs/adr/0029 D4). The UI never calls it.

The state cookie of `GET /auth/oidc/login` must be present, younger than
ten minutes, and hold the `state` the issuer returned. The code is
exchanged with the PKCE verifier; the ID token's signature, issuer,
audience, expiry and nonce are verified (D1); the groups are read from
`COWORK_OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM` — in the ID token, else from UserInfo (D2) —
and must pass the gate: one of them is in `COWORK_OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUPS` or
is `COWORK_ADMIN_GROUP` (docs/adr/0030 D1). The person is found by
issuer and subject, or made (docs/adr/0029 D5), and their memberships
are derived from the teams' group mappings (docs/adr/0030 D2). Then the
session is made as the local login makes it — a new cookie, and the
session the request presented ended (docs/adr/0031 D5) — the state
cookie is cleared, and the answer is `303` to `return_to`.

Every failure is `303` to `/login?error=<code>&return=<return_to>`, the
state cookie cleared and no session made. `return` is the path the login
began with, for the page's next attempt: it is there when the state
cookie still opens, stale or not, and the path is not `/`, the page's
default. The codes: `oidc_failed` — the state cookie is missing, stale
or does not match, the exchange or the verification failed, or the
issuer answered a login that was not silent with `error`;
`login_required` — the issuer answered a silent login
(`silent=true`) with `error` — `login_required`,
`interaction_required`, `consent_required`,
`account_selection_required` or any other, since the person did not ask
for that attempt — when the state cookie still opens, stale or not
(docs/adr/0029 D6); `not_allowed` — the person is outside the
gate, or deactivated (docs/adr/0024 D5); `not_initialised` — no team
exists and the person is not in `COWORK_ADMIN_GROUP` (docs/adr/0032 D5);
`oidc_unavailable` — no identity provider is configured. A refused
login is recorded (docs/adr/0026); the reason reaches the log, never the
page, and neither ever holds a code or a token. A silent login that
comes back with a code is a login like any, refused by the same codes.

The issuer may add parameters this document does not name, such as `iss`
(RFC 9207) or `session_state`: the route takes them and reads none of
them (`x-cowork-open-query`).

post.description:
Sets the session cookie `__Host-cowork-session` (`HttpOnly; Secure;
SameSite=Lax; Path=/`) and answers whether the password is temporary
and must be changed before anything else (docs/adr/0033 D4). A new
session is made at every login, and the one the request presented is
ended (docs/adr/0031 D5).

Every failure is the same `401 invalid_credentials` in the same time —
an unknown username, a wrong password, a locked or a deactivated
account — so neither the answer nor the lockout says whether an account
exists (docs/adr/0033 D6). `COWORK_LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES` (5) failures of one
username within fifteen minutes lock it; more attempts from one client
address within a minute than `COWORK_LOGIN_ADDRESS_LIMIT` (20) allows are
`429 too_many_attempts` — the client being the TCP peer, or behind
`COWORK_TRUSTED_PROXIES` the first address of `X-Forwarded-For`, from the
right, that is not one of them (docs/adr/0035 D2). While no
team exists, only a global administrator may log in: anyone else, with
the right password, gets `403 not_initialised` and no session
(docs/adr/0032 D5).

There is no session yet to carry a CSRF check, so the request must come
from `COWORK_BASE_URL`: its `Origin`, or without one its `Referer`, has
to equal it, else `403 csrf` (docs/adr/0037 D5).

post.description:
Deletes the session's row and clears the cookie (docs/adr/0031 D4). A
write of a session, so the CSRF check applies: a page of another site
cannot log a person out (docs/adr/0037 D5).

A session the identity provider made, whose issuer names an
`end_session_endpoint` in its discovery, answers `200` with
`end_session_url`: the issuer's logout with `client_id` and
`post_logout_redirect_uri` = `COWORK_BASE_URL` + `/login`, where the
browser goes next to end its session at the issuer as well (D4). The
ID token was not kept (D1), so the URL carries no `id_token_hint`. Every
other logout answers `204`.

get.description:
A navigation of the browser — the login page's button sets
`window.location` here — and never a call: the answer is a redirect
(docs/adr/0029 D1). With an identity provider configured it is `302` to
the issuer's authorization endpoint, for the authorization code flow
with PKCE (`S256`), a `state` and a `nonce`, and it sets the cookie
`__Host-cowork-oidc` that holds them with `return_to` and whether the
login is silent for the callback.
Without one, or while its gate admits nobody — the cases in which
`GET /auth/options` answers `oidc: false` — it is `303` to
`/login?error=oidc_unavailable&return=<return_to>`.

`return_to` is where the browser lands after the login: a path of this
installation that starts with `/`, not with `//` or `/\`, holds no
control character and is at most 2048 characters long. Anything else,
or none, is `/`; it is never refused, so a bad link still leads to a
login.

`silent=true` is the login page signing the person in again by itself,
after their session ended (docs/adr/0029 D6): the authorization request
carries `prompt=none` (OIDC Core 1.0 3.1.2.1), so an issuer that still
holds a session of the person answers with a code at once — the login
then completes like any — and one that would have to show a page
answers with an error, which the callback turns into
`/login?error=login_required`. An issuer that ignores `prompt=none`
shows its own form, as for any login. The page's button never sends
it.

No credential: whoever comes here has none yet. Nothing is decided here
that a forged link could abuse — the session is made by the callback,
and only for the browser that holds the state cookie this answer set.
